speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the presence of grunting and retractions suggests significant work of breathing. Have you noticed any frothy fluid coming from the nose or mouth, and is your baby passing urine? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray findings of a "ground glass" appearance with reticular granularity are classic for Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). Given your newborn status, do you recall if you had a C-section or if your mother had diabetes? REQUEST TEST: Blood_Gas_Analysis
